processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds, movable stepwise inside the furnace, were successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast, the remaining melt composition in the ingot was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500-mm-long sheets

processing_steps.method: cutting perpendicular to the rolling direction into segments
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cut into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure after hot rolling and water quenching, with some retained microsegregations of Mn; XRD screening indicates increasing ferrite content with Al in the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl system.

phases_present.volume_fraction: increases with Al content in the 2–11 wt.% range

defects.type: no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations observed in the final materials

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: phase characterization / screening of constituting phases
characterization_methods.key_findings: For Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl, increasing ferrite content with Al; ferrite content is more relevant for the mechanical trend than the presence of κ-carbides or ε-martensite.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements for every material state
characterization_methods.key_findings: For Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl, yield strength and ultimate tensile strength both increase while tensile elongation drops with Al content in the 2–11 wt.% range.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; as-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling and water quenching resulted in a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl TWIP steel family, bulk screening shows that yield strength and ultimate tensile strength both increase while tensile elongation drops with increasing Al content in the 2–11 wt.% range; this qualitative trend is the only mechanical information attributable to the family, since specific numeric values for the 550 °C/1 h aged condition are not individually reported (block b0026).

Figure 6 plots mechanical and XRD phase-fraction data for the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl group only for as-quenched, 400 °C/24 h, 500 °C/24 h, and 600 °C/24 h conditions; the 550 °C/1 h condition of this sample is not among the plotted series, so no numeric YS/UTS/TE/hardness or phase-fraction values can be attributed to it (figure_006).

XRD screening of the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl samples indicates that the increasing ferrite content with Al is more relevant for the observed mechanical trend than the presence of κ-carbides or ε-martensite (block b0026).
